items.t: English Bluff is the west shore of Tsawwassen, in the City of Delta, running along English Bluff Road from 12 Avenue south to 1 Avenue and the Strait of Georgia shore, around English Bluff Elementary School at 402 English Bluff Road; exact City boundary lines for the name are not verified, and "English Bluff" is not confirmed as a standalone official City of Delta neighbourhood name — Tsawwassen is the Official Community Plan community area.

The defining landmarks are Fred Gingell Park, 253 English Bluff Rd (picnic tables, trails, viewpoint, and stairs from the upper park down to the beach), and Diefenbaker Park, 5579 1 Ave (playgrounds, trails, viewpoint, washrooms, water park).

Transit on the bluff itself is community-shuttle scale: route 604 English Bluff / Bridgeport Station runs via 56 Street, 16 Avenue, Beach Grove Road, 12 Avenue, English Bluff Road and 1 Avenue with peak service to Bridgeport Station, and the 614 English Bluff shuttle loops via 1 Avenue, English Bluff Road and 12 Avenue from South Delta Exchange.

Where condo stock concentrates: it does not concentrate here at all. The Delta Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 8400, focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs — all outside English Bluff.

Schools for the sample address 402 English Bluff Road, from the SD37 School Locator: English Bluff Elementary (K–7), 402 English Bluff Rd, and South Delta Secondary (8–12), 750 53 St; SD37 has no middle-school category, and catchments for other addresses are not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in English Bluff

items.t: Development Permit Area SD2 — the rule that defines this shore: OCP Bylaw No. 8400 names "SD2 English Bluff (Tsawwassen Escarpment)," Category "b" (protection of development from hazardous conditions): the waterfront area is subject to mud flows, debris flows, erosion, land slip and subsidence, the ocean-frontage slopes are subject to erosion, and existing vegetation and tree cover on the slopes must be protected.

SD2 building rules: no building with the underside of a wooden floor system, or the top of a concrete slab for habitation, business or storage of goods damageable by floodwaters, lower than the Flood Construction Level (unless a lesser elevation is set by the provincial ministry); no building within 7.5 m of the natural boundary of the sea or within 7.5 m of the inboard toe of any dike; a restrictive covenant acknowledging the land may be subject to flooding is required; and development affected by hazardous conditions is subject to conditions set by a suitably qualified Professional Engineer.

The beach is not part of the lot: Delta states foreshore and water use is interjurisdictional (federal Fisheries Act, provincial Water Sustainability Act and Riparian Areas Regulation, flood protection requirements and Delta bylaws), and the foreshore below the natural boundary is Crown land administered through FrontCounter BC.

Delta zoning and plan: housing sits under Delta Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 (RS zones on this shore); the current OCP is the consolidated Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 8400 (2024) — it has no lettered schedules and no Tsawwassen area-plan schedule (the old Tsawwassen Area Plan was Schedule D.1 under the previous OCP, Bylaw No. 3950), and farm land in the plan is designated "Agriculture (A)."

SSMUH (the only route to small strata-type product here): Delta's Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing amendments — Zoning Amendment Bylaws No. 8394 and 8395, adopted June 24, 2024 — amended Zoning Bylaws No. 7600 and No. 2750 to permit SSMUH on properties that permit single detached or duplex dwellings; Delta's notice to the Province states the bylaws allow four units on all residential properties in the City, and six units on properties within 400 m of frequent transit along Scott Road (Scott Road is in North Delta, not Tsawwassen). On this shore the SD2 hazard conditions still sit on top of that permission.

Form B (applies the moment a buyer looks at a strata unit inland): under the Strata Property Act, s. 59, the Form B: Information Certificate discloses the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still to be paid, the contingency reserve fund (CRF) balance net of approved expenditures, and a summary of the strata's insurance; the rules, current budget, any owner-developer Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report must be attached. The strata must provide it within 7 days of request; the maximum charge is $35 plus up to 25 cents per page for copying. Since 2023, Form Bs must also provide summaries of strata insurance and electrical planning reports.

Depreciation reports are no longer waivable for most stratas: regulations in force July 1, 2024 require strata corporations with five or more strata lots to obtain a depreciation report every five years, and the report can no longer be deferred by a vote; reports carry a 30-year projection of repair and replacement costs and three CRF cash-flow models.

Rental-restriction bylaws are void province-wide: as of Nov 24, 2022, no strata corporation may have a residential rental-restriction bylaw — all existing ones are invalid, with no bylaw amendment needed. Stratas may still ban or limit short-term rentals by bylaw.

Age bylaws — only 55+ survives: under the Strata Property Act, ss. 123.1 and 123.2, a strata may restrict residents to age 55 or older; any age bylaw below 55 has been invalid since Nov 24, 2022. The bylaw restricts who may live in the unit, not who may own it.

Newly built home exemption (not first-time-only): full PTT exemption threshold $1,100,000 fair market value, phasing out over the $50,000 range above it and fully eliminated at $1,150,000 (effective Apr 1, 2024); a unit in a newly built condo building not occupied since construction can qualify.

GST on new construction only: the first-time home buyers' GST/HST rebate (Bill C-4, royal assent Mar 13, 2026) together with the GST/HST new housing rebate returns 100% of the GST on a newly constructed or substantially renovated home valued up to $1 million, gradually reduced between $1 million and $1.5 million, none at $1.5 million or more, maximum $50,000, for agreements in the Mar 20, 2025–2031 window; the older new housing rebate alone is 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.
CMHC mortgage loan insurance premiums: on the published homeowner schedule run from 0.60% of the loan (loan-to-value up to 65%) to 4.50% (90.01%–95% LTV with a non-traditional down payment).

blocks.text: Good to know about English Bluff

items.t: The OCP deliberately steers growth away from this shore. Bylaw No. 8400 focuses Tsawwassen growth on the Urban Centre, the 56 Street corridor, Southlands and Tsawwassen Springs — a named major project inside English Bluff is not verified, because the plan does not put one there.

The flood covenant runs with the land. SD2's guidelines require a restrictive covenant acknowledging the land may be subject to flooding — it will show on title and bind the next owner, which is why bluff listings have to be read title-first.

The stairs at Fred Gingell Park are the public beach access for the upper bluff — a City report states stairs run from the upper park at 253 English Bluff Rd down to the beach, which matters to homes on the landward side with no stairs of their own.

Delta's flood system is municipal-scale, and the bluff is its edge case: the City operates and maintains over 63 km of flood protection infrastructure, 31 drainage pump stations and approximately 538 km of drainage infrastructure — but SD2 lots carry site-specific engineer-set conditions on top of that system.

The RS3 lot standard explains why there is no condo product to find: a 4,000 m² minimum subdivision lot area (estate-scale by Delta standards, where the wider Bylaw 7600 ladder starts at RS7's 335 m²) keeps this shore in large detached lots.

Health care is inland: Delta Hospital, 5800 Mountain View Boulevard in Ladner, is the nearest hospital, and Fraser Health lists a South Delta After-Hours Urgent and Primary Care Centre at 1826-4949 Canoe Pass Way in Tsawwassen.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in English Bluff

items.t: Fee-simple is the tenure that exists here — plainly: A detached house on the bluff is fee-simple: there is NO strata corporation, NO Form B, and NO strata fees. The buyer's diligence is municipal — zoning, the SD2 development permit area below, covenants on title — plus any homeowners-association terms if a specific lot carries them (none verified area-wide: Not confirmed).
OCP: Bylaw No. 8400 (2024): The current OCP is a single consolidated plan — it contains NO lettered schedules. Farm land in the plan is designated "Agriculture (A)".

SSMUH (the only route to small multi-unit product here): Delta adopted its small-scale multi-unit housing zoning amendments as Bylaws 8394 and 8395 on June 24, 2024, allowing up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots city-wide, subject to the bylaw and to any hazard or streamside permit area on the lot. On this shore the SD2 hazard conditions sit on top of that permission; SSMUH product is typically fee-simple or bare-land in form, and strata conversion would be a separate step — do not market a future SSMUH build as a "townhouse complex" until its tenure is registered.

Strata rules that apply the moment a buyer looks at a townhouse inland: Form B (Strata Property Act s. 59): discloses monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still to be paid, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget and most recent depreciation report attached; the strata must provide it within 7 days of request, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Since July 1, 2024 a strata with five or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every five years and cannot vote to defer it (a strata under five lots sits UNDER that threshold); since November 1, 2023 the CRF must receive a minimum of 10% of the annual operating fund each year.

Rental and age bylaws (inland strata): Every BC strata rental-restriction bylaw has been invalid since Nov 24, 2022 — a directory "rentals not allowed" line for an inland Tsawwassen building is VOID in-entry. Under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1 and 123.2 only a 55+ age bylaw is valid (with the May 1, 2023 exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, defined children, legacy residents and live-in caregivers); that is the framework behind The Lexington's and Tsawwassen Greene's 55+ rules in Tsawwassen Central.

GST and rebates (new construction only): Resale homes carry no GST. On a new home, the first-time home buyers' GST/HST rebate (Bill C-4, Royal Assent March 13, 2026, per CRA News No. 122) rebates 100% of the GST up to $1 million (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, for agreements in the March 20, 2025–2031 window; the older GST New Housing Rebate is 36% of the GST, maximum $6,300, phasing out between $350,000 and $450,000.

Property transfer tax and buyer programs: General PTT is 1% on the first $200,000, 2% from $200,000 to $2 million, 3% above $2 million, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3 million — a page's "Over $3M — 5%" row is a compression of that 3% + 2% and is flagged as such wherever met. The first-time buyers' exemption removes the tax on the first $500,000 (maximum saving $8,000) at $835,000 or less, phasing out to $860,000, and the newly built home exemption is full to $1,100,000, phasing out by $1,150,000. The Home Buyers' Plan allows up to $60,000 per person from RRSPs, the First Home Savings Account $8,000 per year to a $40,000 lifetime limit, and CMHC homeowner premiums run 0.6%–4.5% of the loan.

faq.a: The city-wide SSMUH permission (up to four units on single-detached and duplex lots) applies on paper, but on this shore the SD2 hazard conditions sit on top of it: A Professional Engineer's conditions, the Flood Construction Level, 7.5 m setbacks from the natural boundary of the sea, and a registered restrictive covenant.
faq.q: Delta allows four units on a duplex lot — can I build a duplex on the bluff?

faq.a: Not the upland owner: The foreshore below the natural boundary is Crown land, and Delta notes foreshore use is interjurisdictional — do not market private beach ownership, stairs or docks without checking tenure.
faq.q: Who owns the beach below a waterfront house?

faq.a: The SD2 justification requires protection of existing vegetation and tree cover on the ocean-frontage slopes — tree removal for a view can need approvals and can affect the slope itself.
faq.q: Can I clear the slope trees for a better view?
